verdictReason: All nine iteration-3 items (CRIT-14..CRIT-22) are resolved, and the code claims behind them were verified on 2026-10-06. PO-9 closes CRIT-18. The case-blind matcher closes CRIT-14 by construction: ASCII lowercase runs before segmentation, so the result cannot depend on case. Every row in the §3.5 table was walked through steps 1-7 and gives the stated result and token. No regressions were found in the save paths, the v2 principal flow, the error contract or requirements.json. Remaining: three LOW items, all auto-fixable. CRIT-23: the substring clause is not written into PO-9. CRIT-24: the case table omits the false-positive classes the substring rule creates. CRIT-25: implementation details. The open B1/B2 items (OQ-18 a-e, including the structured variableNames body and the D7 re-rulings) are explicitly gated on @architect and block only B1/B2. Weighted average 4.38.

issues.description: The substring rule goes further than the recorded PO-9 text. requirements.json#poDecisions PO-9 says 'a name triggers if any of its TOKENS is an identity token'. The case-blind, inside-letter-run substring search (spec §3.5 step 5) is listed in spec Metadata as a @pm auto-decision made for CRIT-14. Without camelCase boundaries it matches across word joins that PO-2/PO-9 tokenization would split. Examples: logInterval [log, interval], useRetry [use, retry], serviceMail [service, mail]. The lead's brief describes PO-9 as including the substring rule, so this is not a design objection. Only the written record is missing.
issues.location: requirements.json#poDecisions PO-9; spec.md#3.5 step 5, Metadata Article IV note
issues.suggestion: Add one clause to PO-9 (or a PO-9a): 'matching is case-blind substring search inside ASCII letter runs; cross-word joins in camelCase/compact names (e.g. LOGINTERVAL, useRetry, voicemail) trigger'. Cite the false-positive classes listed in this entry.

issues.description: The shared case table (§3.5, identity-name-cases.json) covers in-word false positives (SUPERUSER, MAX_USERS) and token-level ones (LOGIN_URL, USER_AGENT, EMAIL_SUBJECT). It omits two classes the substring rule creates. (1) Cross-word joins with no separator, where the matcher sees one letter run: '...use'+'r...' gives useRef, useRetry, focusError, mouseRight, pauseResume, reuseResult (user). '...log'+'in...' gives logInfo, logIndex, logInterval, logInput, blogIndex/BLOGINDEX, catalogInfo, dialogInput (login). '...e'+'mail...' gives voicemail, serviceMail, invoiceMail, storeMail (email). (2) Separator asymmetry: LOG_INTERVAL, INVOICE_MAIL and USE_RETRY do not match, while LOGINTERVAL, invoiceMail and USERETRY do. Other English words containing 'user' are missing too: TROUSERS, ACCUSER, ABUSER, CAUSER, DIFFUSER. The table also does not pin the exact-segment reading of the merges: a prefix reading would merge SOE_IDENTITY into soeid. E_MAILBOX covers this for e+mail only. No natural false-positive class was found for 'soeid' (SHOE_ID and shoeId do not contain it).
issues.suggestion: Add these rows with their expected results: match/user for USERETRY, useRef, focusError; match/login for LOGINTERVAL, logInfo, BLOGINDEX, catalogInfo; match/email for VOICEMAIL, serviceMail; match/user for TROUSERS; no match for LOG_INTERVAL, INVOICE_MAIL, USE_RETRY, SOE_IDENTITY. The PO then sees the cost in the artifact that pins the behaviour, and any later narrowing is a deliberate matcherVersion bump.

iterations.orderingAndRequiredFieldAssessment: SOUND, with one labelling error. Putting the ack check after the 403 and after the strict parse keeps NFR-4: authorization still decides first, and an absent test still gives 403 (C3 :127). A required field cannot break a live client, because the only caller is the flag-gated SecretInput (CON-2). Records do not fail on a missing component, so null -> SECRET_ACK_REQUIRED works as D7 says. The labelling error is that 'behind a disabled flag' is true only for the FRONTEND. StudioSecretsController is @Profile("!worker") and always mapped. With studio.secrets.vault.provider=none (default), a create today answers 503 VAULT_NOT_CONFIGURED. After this change, an unacknowledged body answers 400 SECRET_ACK_REQUIRED first. That is a live status-semantic change on a public route in every deployment, which is exactly why ADR-002 §34.1 makes it Class C. The spec handles the governance correctly, but its 'dark' wording (§2.1, CON-2 impact, §7 skew risk 'Low now (dark)') understates the change.

issues.description: §1 Overview says: 'An author who stores a personal credential anyway does so through an explicit, recorded acknowledgment.' On the only path live in the alpha (plain variables, FR-3/FR-4, D3/D4/R4) there is no acknowledgment and nothing is recorded, by design. The acknowledgment and the audit exist only on the dark Vault dialog. The user's 'they can add on their own risk' is therefore advisory-only in the alpha, and the spec never says so plainly. On top of that, plainVariableGuidance.alpha tells authors to 'avoid tests that need a password for now', which pulls against the own-risk allowance the product owner granted.
issues.suggestion: Reword the overview: 'On the Vault path (dark until vaultSecrets is on), personal credentials need an explicit, recorded acknowledgment. On plain variables (live), the guidance is advisory only; own risk is implicit and unrecorded.' Add a non-goal or open question: 'No acknowledgment on plain variables (R4).' Flag for @pm whether 'avoid tests that need a password' matches the own-risk decision, or should read 'if you must, use a functional ID; personal credentials are at your own risk.'

iterations.verdictReason: The iteration-3 redesign (name-triggered, A/B1/B2 slices, transient top-level list) is sound, and its central claim holds. 'Exempt until added/renamed' can be determined on the server from the save request: both update paths CAS both revisions under a row lock, and any variables difference bumps configurationRevision, so the FE's loaded variables equal the server's stored variables for every save that passes STALE_REVISION. No HIGH issues. Seven MEDIUM: surface-dependent matcher results caused by upper-casing (CRIT-14); a missed fourth save path, Run (CRIT-15); no principal on the v2 update path (CRIT-16); error-contract gaps (CRIT-17); the head-word narrowing of PO-2 unconfirmed by the PO (CRIT-18); stale superseded references in requirements.json and AC-10 (CRIT-19); and existing @architect rulings silently reversed (CRIT-20). issues.description: The matcher result depends on the surface for the same author input. The Studio page (ChecksStudioPage.tsx:1268) and the wizard (UiTestConfig.tsx:73, CreateCheckPage.tsx:116) upper-case names, so the camelCase boundaries never apply there, and the merge (step 2) and strip (step 3) steps never see a compact name. Worked through §3.5: `emailAddress` matches in the Vault dialog ([email,address] -> merge -> email) but becomes EMAILADDRESS on the Studio page, a single token where R3 fails because the head ends in 'address'. So it is a miss there, even though EMAIL_ADDRESS is a table 'match' row. The same split happens for USERNAMEUAT / LOGINIDDEV / SOEIDVALUE versus USERNAME_UAT (match). Other ambiguous or unlisted cases: 'user|login|soe followed by id|name' also produces 'soename', which is not in the listed outputs. USER_2_NAME merges across a dropped digit token into 'username'. E_MAIL and eMail tokenize to [e,mail], so no match. EMAIL_ID is a no-match (head 'id'), although it is a common spelling of the email login. LAST_LOGIN is a match, but it is usually a timestamp. A mixed-case 'USERname' splits to [use,rname]. Two parity hazards are not pinned: Java String.toLowerCase() without Locale.ROOT (under a Turkish locale 'LOGIN' becomes 'logın'), and Unicode versus ASCII case classes for the boundary rules.
issues.suggestion: Make the result independent of case: run R3's suffix test after removing a trailing neutral word or merge partner from a compact head (or add 'emailaddress'/'emailaddr' to I), or state in §3.5 that compact misses are accepted (CON-4). Put every case named here into identity-name-cases.json with an explicit expected result, including null/empty/whitespace names. Require Locale.ROOT lowercasing and ASCII-only character classes in both implementations. List the merge outputs exhaustively.

issues.description: FR-12 says 'every save action' is gated, but D16, AC-15, T-FE-15 and §9 list three Save buttons and miss a fourth save path. RunControl is wired with onSaveBeforeRun={saveDraft} (ChecksStudioPage.tsx:769), so pressing Run on a dirty draft saves it. With D16's early-return guard, Run on a draft with a pending acknowledgment fails, and nothing specifies the guard's return value (SaveOutcome is 'saved'|'error'|'conflict'), how RunControl reacts, or a visible reason at the Run control. That breaks FR-12's 'visible reason' and NFR-2 (G155).

issues.description: The v2 update path has no principal at the point where D17 implies the rule runs. updateAuthoringDraft authorizes in lockForAuthoringWrite (StudioService.java:719-737) and then delegates with updateTest(id, metadataOnly, null) (:352), so auth is null inside updateTest. If IdentityNameAckPolicy is called from updateTest, which is the shared create/update path that 'pass the field through metadataOnly' (C19) implies, the v2 audit line has no principal (FR-8/PO-4), and the identity lookup (extractIdentity) has nothing to read. T-BE-12 checks only that the field is accepted and the rule runs, not that the audit line names the principal. Separately, C20's 'every StudioService public method runs in a transaction' is not accurate: compileTest, confirmCompile, executeTest and cancelExecution are Propagation.NOT_SUPPORTED (:620, :663, :959, :996). This is harmless for the save paths, which are all @Transactional, but it is overstated.

issues.description: The error contract for B1 has four gaps. (a) ErrorResponse is {error, message} only (openapi.yaml:2487-2492; ChecksExceptionHandler.java:233-236), so the names in IDENTITY_NAME_ACK_REQUIRED exist only in human text. The §7 mitigation for matcher drift ('a server-side match the FE missed yields a deterministic 400 naming the variable') leaves the author stuck: the FE shows no checkbox for that row, so renaming is the only way out. This is reachable whenever an MFE bundle cached in the shell lags a matcherVersion bump. (b) A malformed list has no assigned code: non-array, missing or extra item fields, more than 100 items, variableName over 64, blank disclaimerVersion. If it is validated in LegacyDeserializer, the 400 comes from StudioController -> authoringMapper.legacy(), before authorization, which contradicts NFR-4 'always after authorization'. (c) An unknown or blank version on a required entry: D17 implies IDENTITY_NAME_ACK_REQUIRED, but T-BE-7 says only '400'. (d) Duplicate rows with the same matching name: if the FE sends one entry per ticked row, the save gets 400 INVALID_IDENTITY_NAME_ACK (duplicate). The spec does not say the FE dedupes by name or that `required` is a set of distinct names.
issues.location: spec.md#3.2 D17, #3.3 server messages, #6.1 T-BE-7, #7 drift row
issues.suggestion: (a) Either add a structured names list to the 400 (a further contract change, for @architect under OQ-18), or state that renaming is the only recovery and remove the §7 mitigation claim. In either case, have the FE re-run its own matcher and show the checkbox for the named rows. (b) Assign INVALID_IDENTITY_NAME_ACK to all shape errors and state where in the order they occur. Prefer validating shape inside the service policy, after authorization, and having the deserializer only carry raw nodes. (c) Pin IDENTITY_NAME_ACK_REQUIRED for unknown or blank versions on required names in T-BE-7. (d) The FE sends at most one entry per distinct name, and the server computes `required` as a set.

falsePositiveClasses: Token-level (PO-9, in the table): LOGIN_URL, LOGIN_PAGE, LOGIN_BUTTON, LAST_LOGIN, USER_AGENT, USER_ROLE, USER_TOKEN, EMAIL_SUBJECT, MAX_USERS. Typical UI-test config names, so these are expected to be the most frequent.
In-word 'user' (partly in the table, SUPERUSER only): TROUSERS, ACCUSER, ABUSER, CAUSER, DIFFUSER, MOUSER, PERUSER.

Cross-word joins in camelCase or compact names (NOT in the table): 'use|r' gives useRef, useRetry, focusError, mouseRight, pauseResume, reuseResult (user); 'log|in' gives logInfo, logIndex, logInterval, logInput, blogIndex/BLOGINDEX, catalogInfo, dialogInput (login); 'e|mail' gives voicemail, serviceMail, invoiceMail, storeMail (email).

Separator asymmetry (NOT in the table): LOG_INTERVAL, INVOICE_MAIL and USE_RETRY do not match, while LOGINTERVAL, invoiceMail and USERETRY do. The result is case-independent but depends on separators.
'soeid': no natural class found (SHOE_ID and shoeId do not contain it). 'account': exact-segment rule, so no substring false positives.

issues.description: The substring rule goes further than the recorded PO-9 text. requirements.json#poDecisions PO-9 says 'a name triggers if any of its TOKENS is an identity token'. The case-blind, inside-letter-run substring search (spec §3.5 step 5) is listed in spec Metadata as a @pm auto-decision made for CRIT-14. Without camelCase boundaries it matches across word joins that PO-2/PO-9 tokenization would split. Examples: logInterval [log, interval], useRetry [use, retry], serviceMail [service, mail]. The lead's brief describes PO-9 as including the substring rule, so this is not a design objection. Only the written record is missing.
issues.location: requirements.json#poDecisions PO-9; spec.md#3.5 step 5, Metadata Article IV note
issues.suggestion: Add one clause to PO-9 (or a PO-9a): 'matching is case-blind substring search inside ASCII letter runs; cross-word joins in camelCase/compact names (e.g. LOGINTERVAL, useRetry, voicemail) trigger'. Cite the false-positive classes listed in this entry.

issues.description: The shared case table (§3.5, identity-name-cases.json) covers in-word false positives (SUPERUSER, MAX_USERS) and token-level ones (LOGIN_URL, USER_AGENT, EMAIL_SUBJECT). It omits two classes the substring rule creates. (1) Cross-word joins with no separator, where the matcher sees one letter run: '...use'+'r...' gives useRef, useRetry, focusError, mouseRight, pauseResume, reuseResult (user). '...log'+'in...' gives logInfo, logIndex, logInterval, logInput, blogIndex/BLOGINDEX, catalogInfo, dialogInput (login). '...e'+'mail...' gives voicemail, serviceMail, invoiceMail, storeMail (email). (2) Separator asymmetry: LOG_INTERVAL, INVOICE_MAIL and USE_RETRY do not match, while LOGINTERVAL, invoiceMail and USERETRY do. Other English words containing 'user' are missing too: TROUSERS, ACCUSER, ABUSER, CAUSER, DIFFUSER. The table also does not pin the exact-segment reading of the merges: a prefix reading would merge SOE_IDENTITY into soeid. E_MAILBOX covers this for e+mail only. No natural false-positive class was found for 'soeid' (SHOE_ID and shoeId do not contain it).
issues.suggestion: Add these rows with their expected results: match/user for USERETRY, useRef, focusError; match/login for LOGINTERVAL, logInfo, BLOGINDEX, catalogInfo; match/email for VOICEMAIL, serviceMail; match/user for TROUSERS; no match for LOG_INTERVAL, INVOICE_MAIL, USE_RETRY, SOE_IDENTITY. The PO then sees the cost in the artifact that pins the behaviour, and any later narrowing is a deliberate matcherVersion bump.

issues.description: Implementation details left out of the B1/Slice A file lists. (a) UITestRequest is a 9-component record (UITestRequest.java:31-40). Adding a JsonNode component breaks every 'new UITestRequest(' call: StudioService.java:341 (metadataOnly) plus about 28 in 15 test files (ConfigurationRevisionTest 5, LegacyStudioAdapterTest 3, TargetPolicyGapTest 3, StudioScheduleApiIT 3, ...). (b) AckSubject.environment on update is not specified: the request's environment or the stored row's? On create it can only be the request's. (c) RunControl already renders run-blocked-reason for !hasSteps and for 'waiting' (RunControl.tsx:268-290). The precedence of blockedReason against those captions is not stated, so two elements with the same test id can render. RunControl has no co-located test file today (only run/runGate.test.tsx), and C23/§5.2 omit the run/ directory. (d) T-BE-6's 'new Locale("tr","TR")' is deprecated on Java 21. Use Locale.of("tr","TR") and restore the default in finally.
issues.suggestion: (a) Add the call sites to §5.2, or keep a 9-arg compatibility constructor that passes null. (b) Use the stored row's environment, read before setEnvironment, for consistency with csiId, or state the choice. (c) blockedReason wins over the waiting caption; with no steps, show the no-steps caption. Write the test in a new frontend/src/components/studio/run/RunControl.test.tsx or in runGate.test.tsx. (d) Use Locale.of and restore the default in finally.
